name: Slack
summary: Slack app registration is fast and agent-friendly: you can create the whole app from a YAML/JSON manifest (UI or apps.manifest.create API), flip on Public Distribution, and install into any workspace with no Slack review. The slow, optional path is a Slack Marketplace listing (preliminary review up to 10 business days plus functional review up to 10 weeks, and you need 10+ active workspaces first); the real-world blocker is workspace admins who require app approval before members can install.

composio.note: Listed under 'Composio-managed OAuth available' on docs.composio.dev/toolkits/managed-auth, so you can skip app creation entirely by using Composio's shared Slack app. If you bring your own app, register https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback as a Redirect URL and set the same value as oauth_redirect_uri in your Composio auth config.

verdict.difficultyReason: No approval gate for creating, distributing, or installing an app in any workspace; the manifest lets an agent declare scopes, bot user, and redirect URLs in one shot. Difficulty only rises if you need a Marketplace listing or org-wide Enterprise Grid deployment.

approvalWait.note: No Slack review to create or distribute an app. Slack Marketplace listing (optional) is a separate review: up to 10 business days preliminary plus up to 10 weeks functional review.

verdict.timeToFirstToken: ~10-15 min; no approval. Marketplace listing adds 2-12 weeks (optional). Workspace admin approval can add days if the target workspace restricts installs.

prerequisites.text: A Slack account that is a member of a workspace you can develop in (free workspace is fine). Creating an app installs it into this 'development workspace'.
An HTTPS redirect URL. Slack rejects http:// redirect URLs and URLs with a # fragment; there is no documented localhost exception, so use ngrok/Cloudflare Tunnel for local dev.
For the apps.manifest.* API path: an App Configuration Token generated from https://api.slack.com/apps (12-hour lifetime, refreshable via tooling.tokens.rotate).
For a Marketplace listing: a public privacy policy, support contact, TLS 1.2+, request signature verification, and 10+ active workspaces with 10+ weekly active users.

steps.title: Decide bot token vs user token scopes
steps.detail: Bot scopes (oauth_config.scopes.bot, issued as xoxb- tokens) let the app act as its own bot user and survive the installing user leaving; user scopes (scopes.user, xoxp- tokens) act as the installing human. Most agents want bot scopes only; add user scopes only for things a bot cannot do (e.g. search:read).
tips: Scopes are additive across installs and cannot be removed from an existing token without revoking it, so start minimal.
Sign in with Slack (openid/profile/email) user scopes cannot be mixed with non-SIWS scopes in the same authorize request.

steps.title: Draft the app manifest (YAML or JSON)
steps.detail:
Only display_information.name is required; everything else is optional. Declare the bot user, bot scopes, redirect URLs and settings in one file so the whole app is reproducible. Minimal example:

display_information:
  name: My Agent
  description: Posts summaries to channels
features:
  bot_user:
    display_name: my-agent
    always_online: true
oauth_config:
  redirect_urls:
    - https://example.com/slack/oauth/callback
    - https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback
  scopes:
    bot:
      - chat:write
      - channels:read
      - channels:history
      - app_mentions:read
settings:
  event_subscriptions:
    bot_events:
      - app_mention
  socket_mode_enabled: true
  org_deploy_enabled: false
  token_rotation_enabled: false
tips: Event Subscriptions and Interactivity each require either a request_url or socket_mode_enabled: true, or the manifest is rejected as invalid_manifest with a JSON pointer to the bad field.
name max 35 chars; bot display_name max 80 chars using a-z 0-9 - _ . only; redirect_urls max 1000 entries; scopes.bot max 255.

steps.title: Create the app from the manifest
steps.detail: UI path: https://api.slack.com/apps -> Create New App -> From a manifest -> pick the development workspace -> paste YAML/JSON -> Create. API path: generate an App Configuration Token on the same page, then POST apps.manifest.create with the manifest as JSON (use apps.manifest.validate first). The config token is tied to a user+workspace, not an app, and expires after 12 hours.
tips: The UI path needs a logged-in Slack session; the API path needs a human to click Generate Token once, after which an agent can create/update/export apps programmatically with tooling.tokens.rotate keeping the token alive.

steps.title: Collect Client ID, Client Secret, and Signing Secret
steps.detail: On the app's Basic Information page copy Client ID, Client Secret and Signing Secret into your secret store. The signing secret is what you use to verify incoming event/interaction payloads; verification tokens are deprecated.

steps.title: Install to the development workspace and get a first token
steps.detail: OAuth & Permissions -> Install to Workspace. A workspace member clicks Allow and Slack issues a Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-...) immediately, no OAuth server needed for this single-workspace case. Verify with auth.test.
tips: If the development workspace has 'Require approved apps' turned on, this click becomes an approval request to a Workspace Owner instead of an install.

steps.title: Implement the OAuth v2 flow for other workspaces
steps.detail: Send users to https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize?client_id=...&scope=chat:write,channels:read&user_scope=&redirect_uri=...&state=.... On callback, POST the 10-minute code to https://slack.com/api/oauth.v2.access with client_id, client_secret, and the same redirect_uri. Response carries access_token (bot), bot_user_id, team.id, enterprise, and authed_user.access_token (user token, if user scopes were requested).
tips: redirect_uri must exactly match a configured Redirect URL or be a subdirectory of one; scheme/host/port must match. Mismatch returns bad_redirect_uri.
If you configure multiple Redirect URLs you must pass redirect_uri explicitly in both the authorize and access calls; omit it and Slack uses the first configured URL.
Always verify state on return; the docs call a mismatch a forgery.

steps.title: Activate Public Distribution
steps.detail: Manage Distribution -> 'Share Your App with Other Workspaces' -> complete the checklist (OAuth redirect URL present, SSL on all request URLs, etc.) -> Activate Public Distribution. This immediately lets any Slack workspace install the app via your 'Add to Slack' link; Slack performs no review. You can deactivate later, which removes the app from every workspace except the original.
tips: Until this is activated, authorize requests from other workspaces fail with invalid_team_for_non_distributed_app.

steps.title: Optionally enable token rotation (irreversible)
steps.detail: Set settings.token_rotation_enabled: true (or toggle in OAuth & Permissions). Access tokens then expire after 12 hours (expires_in: 43200) and you refresh via oauth.v2.access with grant_type=refresh_token; each refresh token is single-use. Existing long-lived tokens must be exchanged once via oauth.v2.exchange.
tips: Token rotation may not be turned off once it is turned on. Test in a dev app first.
Without rotation, Slack OAuth tokens do not expire; they only die on auth.revoke, uninstall, or user deactivation.

steps.title: Optionally make the app org-ready for Enterprise Grid
steps.detail: Add at least one bot scope, then in Org Level Apps click Opt-In (manifest: settings.org_deploy_enabled: true). An Org Admin/Owner installs at org level; the oauth.v2.access response then has is_enterprise_install: true, team: null and an enterprise.id you should key storage on. After an org install the app is in zero workspaces until the admin adds them, so redirect to https://app.slack.com/manage/ENTERPRISE_ID/integrations/profile/APP_ID/workspaces/add.
tips: Flipping org_deploy_enabled requires existing workspaces to reinstall.
Org-wide tokens cover many workspaces; some Web API methods need an explicit team_id. Use auth.teams.list and the team_access_granted/revoked events to track which workspaces you can reach.

steps.title: Optionally submit to the Slack Marketplace
steps.detail: Only worth it once you have 10+ active workspaces and 10+ weekly active users. Prepare a public privacy policy, support page, per-scope justifications, reviewer test credentials and ideally a demo video, then submit from the app dashboard. Preliminary review takes up to 10 business days; functional review up to 10 weeks for new apps (6 weeks for resubmissions). Published apps cannot simply deactivate distribution; you must discontinue the listing.
tips: Listing also restores Tier 3 rate limits on conversations.history/replies, which unlisted commercial apps created after 2025-05-29 lose (Tier 1: 1 req/min, 15 messages per call).

scopes.note: Slack uses granular bot and user scopes declared in oauth_config.scopes. Nothing triggers a Slack review for an unlisted app; for Marketplace submissions, broad history/search/admin scopes trigger enhanced review and must be justified feature-by-feature.

examples.purpose: Send messages as the bot user (bot scope).
Post to public channels the bot has not joined.
List and view basic info about public channels.
Read message history in public channels the bot is in. Marketplace: *:history scopes trigger enhanced review and need a clear use case.
Receive app_mention events when users @-mention the bot.
Look up users in the workspace.
Read user email addresses; often needed to map Slack users to your own accounts.
User-token search of workspace content. Marketplace: listed as unlikely to be approved without a clear use case and triggers enhanced review.

triggers: Submitting the app for a Slack Marketplace listing (optional; the only Slack-side review).
Installing into a workspace whose owners enabled 'Only allow pre-approved apps' (workspace-side, not Slack-side).
Org-level install on Enterprise Grid, which routes a request to an Org Admin.
approval.process: No Slack review is needed to create, publicly distribute, or install an app in any workspace. For the Marketplace, there are two stages: a preliminary review of listing copy, documentation, scope justifications and installability, then a functional review where reviewers install and test every feature and scope on a non-development workspace.
approval.reviewTime: Marketplace only: preliminary review up to 10 business days; functional review up to 10 weeks for new submissions, up to 6 weeks for changes to published apps. Resubmitting during preliminary review resets your queue position. Cannot be expedited.
reviewerAsksFor: A written justification for every requested scope, limited to features already built and testable.
Test accounts with dummy data plus credentials for any third-party services the app talks to.
A way for reviewers to install the app themselves (Public Distribution must be active).
A video demo covering install, OAuth, setup, end-to-end use and uninstall (strongly recommended).
Public privacy policy (what is collected, how used, retention, deletion, contact) and a public support page.
Evidence of 10+ active workspaces (used in the last 28 days) and 10+ weekly active users.
commonRejections: App not production-ready: bugs, poor UX, test commands left in, or still in private beta.
Missing test credentials or reviewer cannot install the app.
Scopes requested for unbuilt or future features, or non-least-privilege scope choices.
Use of legacy/restricted scopes (admin.*, identity.*, search:read, workflow.steps:execute, triggers:*) without partner status or clear need.
Insecure practices: tokens logged or exposed client-side, no request signature verification, TLS below 1.2.
Privacy policy missing required disclosures or only a physical address as contact.

nuances.title: Redirect URLs must be HTTPS, subdirectory matches allowed
nuances.detail: Both configured Redirect URLs and the redirect_uri you send must use HTTPS; http:// examples are explicitly marked bad and anchors (#) are disallowed. A redirect_uri matches if it equals a configured URL or is a subdirectory of it with identical scheme, host and port. Nothing in the docs permits localhost, so tunnel for local dev.

nuances.title: Tokens never expire unless you opt into rotation
nuances.detail: Default bot/user tokens are long-lived and die only on auth.revoke, uninstall, or user deactivation. Token rotation (12-hour tokens, single-use refresh tokens) is opt-in and cannot be turned off once enabled.

nuances.title: Adding scopes forces a reinstall
nuances.detail: Manifest changes such as new scopes do not affect existing installs until each workspace reinstalls the app. Scopes are additive and cannot be removed from a live token without revoking it.

nuances.title: Unlisted commercial apps get throttled on history reads
nuances.detail: Since 2025-05-29, newly created non-Marketplace commercially distributed apps (and new installs of older ones) are limited to Tier 1 on conversations.history and conversations.replies: about 1 request per minute and max 15 messages per call. Internal custom apps and Marketplace apps keep the old limits.

nuances.title: Workspace admins can gate every install
nuances.detail: Workspace Owners can enable 'Only allow pre-approved apps'; then members either cannot install or must submit a request that owners/app managers approve (optionally via automation rules). Approving a request is approving the app's scopes, so minimal scopes raise approval odds.

nuances.title: Enterprise Grid installs look different
nuances.detail: Org-level installs return is_enterprise_install: true with team: null; key your install store on enterprise.id. The app is in zero workspaces until an admin adds them, and later per-workspace OAuth redirects ignore scope changes because scopes are inherited from the org install.

nuances.title: App Configuration Tokens are per user+workspace and short-lived
nuances.detail: The token used for apps.manifest.create/update/export expires 12 hours after generation and ships with a refresh token for tooling.tokens.rotate. One token can manage all apps you own in that workspace.

nuances.title: Public Distribution is a toggle, not a review
nuances.detail: Activating it only requires completing a self-serve checklist (OAuth redirect URL, SSL on request URLs). Deactivating removes the app from every workspace except the development one; a published Marketplace app instead has to discontinue its listing.

blockers.blocker: Target workspace has 'Only allow pre-approved apps' enabled, so the install button becomes a request or is blocked outright.
blockers.workaround: Have the member submit the in-Slack approval request with a comment, or contact a Workspace Owner/app manager directly; keep scopes minimal since owners approve scopes, not just the app. For Enterprise orgs, ask the Org Admin to pre-approve via admin.apps.approve or the admin UI.

blockers.blocker: No HTTPS endpoint for the redirect URL during local development (Slack rejects http:// and offers no localhost exception).
blockers.workaround: Use an HTTPS tunnel (ngrok, Cloudflare Tunnel) and register that URL, or skip OAuth entirely for the dev workspace by using Install to Workspace plus Socket Mode.

blockers.blocker: Authorize from another workspace fails with invalid_team_for_non_distributed_app.
blockers.workaround: Activate Public Distribution in Manage Distribution; no review is needed.

blockers.blocker: bad_redirect_uri on oauth.v2.access even though the URL looks right.
blockers.workaround: When multiple Redirect URLs are configured, send the identical redirect_uri in both the authorize and oauth.v2.access calls; check scheme/host/port and that the path is the configured one or a subdirectory of it.

blockers.blocker: Agent needs to create/update the app without a browser session.
blockers.workaround: Have a human generate an App Configuration Token once at https://api.slack.com/apps; the agent then uses apps.manifest.validate/create/update/export and tooling.tokens.rotate to keep the token fresh.

blockers.blocker: Marketplace submission refused because the app has fewer than 10 active workspaces / 10 weekly active users.
blockers.workaround: Distribute unlisted first via the Add to Slack link until adoption meets the threshold, then submit. Only security/compliance partners using the Discovery API are exempt.

agentDoes: Choose bot vs user scopes and draft the full YAML/JSON manifest including redirect URLs (your callback plus Composio's https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback if using Composio custom auth).
Run apps.manifest.validate / apps.manifest.create / apps.manifest.update once a human has handed over an App Configuration Token, and keep the token alive with tooling.tokens.rotate.
Generate the Add to Slack authorize URL, implement the callback handler, exchange the code via oauth.v2.access, verify state, and store tokens keyed on team.id or enterprise.id.
Implement refresh logic if token rotation is enabled, and signing-secret verification for events.
Draft Marketplace listing copy, per-scope justifications, privacy policy and support page text.
humanDoes: Log in to Slack and either paste the manifest at https://api.slack.com/apps or click Generate Token for an App Configuration Token.
Click Install to Workspace / Allow in the development workspace and copy Client Secret and Signing Secret into the secret store.
Click Activate Public Distribution and, if needed, Opt-In to Org Level Apps.
Get workspace owners or Enterprise Org Admins to approve the app where install approval is enforced.
Accept the Marketplace agreement, record the demo video, hand reviewers test credentials, and respond to review feedback.

tested: Opened every docs.slack.dev page listed above on 2026-10-23 and confirmed api.slack.com/authentication/oauth-v2, /reference/manifests, /distribution, /slack-marketplace/review-guide and /authentication/rotation all 302-redirect to docs.slack.dev.
Confirmed the manifest reference marks only display_information.name as required and lists token_rotation_enabled, org_deploy_enabled and socket_mode_enabled under settings.
Confirmed the Marketplace review guide currently states 10 active workspaces (a changelog entry mentioned a reduction to 5, but the live guideline page still says 10).
Confirmed docs.composio.dev/toolkits/managed-auth lists SLACK under Composio-managed OAuth available.

Confirmed on docs.slack.dev/slack-marketplace/slack-marketplace-review-guide (spot-check 2026-10-23): 'the preliminary part of the review takes up to 10 business days', 'the functional review takes up to 10 weeks for new submissions and 6 weeks for published apps resubmitting changes', and 'Your app has been installed on 10 or more active workspaces' (active = used in the past 28 days). The review guide itself does not mention the 10 weekly-active-users figure; that comes from the guidelines page, which lists apps 'installed on less than 10 active workspaces and have less than 10 weekly active users' as unsuitable.

Confirmed on docs.slack.dev/authentication/using-token-rotation (spot-check 2026-10-23): 'With token rotation, it expires every 12 hours' / 'always expire in 43,200 seconds'; 'Refresh tokens are designed to be used once'; 'Token rotation may not be turned off once it's turned on'.

Confirmed on docs.slack.dev/changelog/2025/05/29/... and the app-manifests page (spot-check 2026-10-23): non-Marketplace commercial apps move from Tier 3 to Tier 1 ('1 request per minute'), 'limit' max/default reduced to 15, effective May 29, 2025 for new apps and new installs; 'Each app configuration token will expire 12 hours after it has been generated' and is refreshed via tooling.tokens.rotate.
